안녕하세요, 여러분. 한국의 가장 큰 명절 중 하나인 설날이 돌아왔어요! 한국에는 새해에 떡국을 먹는 풍습이 있잖아요. 떡국을 먹어야 한 살을 더 먹는다고 하는데, 이번 영상에서는 한국식으로 설날을 보내기 위해서 떡국을 먹어보기로 했어요. 

라라랜드 (Laraland) 에서 온 라라와 함께 우리의 한국인 배우자들을 위해서 떡국 요리에 도전했는데요 저희가 만든 떡국은 "소고기 떡국" 입니다. 라라는 아예 한국 요리를 해 본 것 자체가 처음이었다고 해요. 저도 떡국은 처음 만들어봐서 긴장도 되고 실수도 많이 했지만 정말 재밌는 경험이었어요. 저희가 만든 떡국 맛이 어땠을지 궁금하시면 영상을 끝까지 봐주세요! 

제 아내 수진이와 라라의 남편 케니가 공정하게 떡국 맛을 평가 해주었구요, 결혼 후 한국에서 보내는 명절이 어떤지에 대해서도 짧게 이야기를 나누었습니다. 쿡방은 처음이었는데 어떠셨을지 모르겠어요. 재미있으셨다면 댓글 많이 남겨주세요!!

안녕하세요, 여러분. 미카인코리아의 61번째 비디오를 봐주셔서 감사합니다. 저는 크리스마스를 보내러 오스트리아에 왔어요. 부모님이 계신 도시로 가기 전에 비엔나에서 이틀을 머물렀는데 ,크리스마스마켓 가는 걸 빠뜨릴 수 없겠죠? 그래서 비엔나의 리스마스마켓 중에 가장 경치가 좋은 곳 중에 하나인 쉔브룬 궁전으로 가 봤습니다. 불행히도 날씨가 좋지 않았지만 수잔네와 알리스가 함께 해줘서 즐거운 시간을 보낼 수 있었어요. 

친구들과 같이 다른 종류의 푼치 (글루바인, 와인에 과일과 허브 등을 넣어 따뜻하게 먹는 음료)를 맛보고, 오스트리아의 전통/특산 음식들도 맛보았어요. 케제녹클 (Käsenockerl), 구운 감자 (Ofen Kartoffel) 그리고 디저트로는 자두잼 카이저쉬만 (Kaiserschmarrn)을 먹었어요. 오스트리아에서는 흔하게 먹는 음식들이랍니다. 오스트리아 크리스마스마켓 특집 먹방을 재미있게 봐주시면 좋겠어요. 궁금하신 것이 있으시면 댓글로 알려주세요.

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to the 49th video of Mika in Korea. And BIG sorry for not uploading any video in September! I went to Austria for over a month to see my family and friends again and also to attend two weddings. And for the wedding of my dear friends Dani & Martin I was even shooting some videos, so I can show it to you in my Youtube channel. Since I was the best man for Martin, I was organizing the Bachelor Party together with Christof, Martin’s 2nd best man! In Austria we call this „Junggesellenabschied“, it is usually the last evening in „freedom“ for the groom, also for the bride, who is celebrating the same with the bridesmaids. For our manly Bachelor Party we went to Tirol to the Area 47, where we spent the full weekend doing fun outdoor activities and having a great party. Of course I can’t show you all the juicy and naughty stuff we did at the evening but I can assure you it was a wild party at the end.

For the wedding Dani and Martin decided to get married in Montenegro, in Herceg Novi. The wedding was held in some kind of vineyard / winery with a breath-talking view. Then we went down through the city, accompanied by a Montenegri Gispy band. At the end we entered a boat and celebrated the wedding-after-party on the sea! Super beautiful and really an awesome wedding. The best, I ever attended and hard to beat for future wedding celebrations.

I hope you’ll enjoy my vlog from Europe, showing you how Western people are celebrating the bachelor party and wedding. Hopefully Dani & Martin will visit me soon again in South Korea as well :)

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to the 48th video of Mika in Korea. It is still hot in Seoul and Mika suggest to fight the heat with drinking some makgeolli (막걸리) and eating some assorted jeon / modeumjeon made dish (모듬전) in a local makgeolli bar in Sindorim. Usually you eat that kind of food and drink makgeolli when it rains but Mika couldn’t wait anymore and really wanted to eat this kind of delicious Korean Anju food! And in this video his French friend Sebastian / Seboom joined him for this weeks mukbang / sulbang video :D

The modeum-jeon (모듬전) contained a hugh variations of different jeons. fish jeon (생선전), meat jeon (고기전), zucchini jeon (애호박전), tofu jeon (두부전), mushroom jeon (버섯전), perilla leaf jeon (깻잎전) and autumn squash jeon (단호박전). And they all were extremely delicious!

Besides eating the Korean modeum-jeon (모듬전) and enjyoing two bottles of Makgeolli we also talked shortly about foreigners being lonely in South Korea, sharing own experiences. It isn’t easy for foreigners living in Korea and they feel lonely many times. 

Mika and Sebastian had a lot of fun shooting this kind of video and enjoyed this kind of Korean fried food a lot. Next time they will eat it again when it is finally rainy in Seoul!

This time we followed one of our viewers recommendation and went to a famous Dwaeji Galbi Restaurant, where we enjoyed some really delicious Korean BBQ. For those who doesn’t know what Dwaeji Galbi (돼지갈비) is, this is grilled pork ribs with a marinated sauce. Of course we had a small chitchat, this time we talked about friendship in Korea & Western countries and the differences in both cultures. 안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to my 43th video of Mika in Korea. This time I met up with my dear friend Dominic from Dom & Hyo and we went to Hongdae to eat some delicious Bossam and enjoy our Friday night. And literally TGIF, since Dom and also me had a pretty rough week behind us and we were both looking forward to enjoy some good food and a few shots of Soju! At the end we decided to order 2 bottles of Soju, so everybody got his own bottle and we really had fun drinking it.

For everybody who doesn’t know what Bossam is. It is a super popular pork dish / pork wrap in Korean cuisine. The meat is served with side dishes such as spicy radish salad, sliced raw garlic, ssamjang (wrap sauce), saeu-jeot (salted shrimp), kimchi, and ssam (wrap) vegetables such as lettuce, kkaennip (perilla leaves), and inner leaves of a napa cabbage. Basically the perfect Korean anju, what means food accompanying alcoholic drinks! To eat the meat you have to wrap it up in a leave together with all the ingredients and eat it with one bite! „bossam“ literally means "wrapped" or "packaged" in Korean.

Besides enjoying this delicious Bossam with Soju, we also talked about the differences about Korean and International marriages! Since Dom and I are both married to Korean woman and we went a lot of time to Korean weddings, we compared in which ways Koreans are different than us westerners. So we talked about how Korean families are different to the USA and Austria, also why they don’t take over the husband’s name, the pressure on a Korean couple after getting married, sharing their income together, making presents to Korean and western parents and how much influence Korean parents take in an marriage as well.

We really had a looooot of fun shooting this video and somehow it is less a mukbang but more a sulbang, a video where it is more about drinking and having a fun time. I am happy that Dom joined me for this video and I hope he will join me soon again!

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to my 42th video of Mika in Korea. And wow, it really got sooo hot these days in South Korea. Especially for me the Korean summer is really tough because it isn’t just hot it is also super humid as well. Austrian summer is also hot these days but more easy going than Korean one. And since I am suffering so much these days because of the heat, my friend Alex and me decided to eat an iconic summer dish, which is super popular in Korea: Samgye-tang (삼계탕) or also called Korean Traditional Ginseng Chicken Soup! For people who don’t know what #Samgyetang is. It is a chicken stuffed with soaked sweet rice (aka glutinous rice). Garlic, ginger, and jujubes (dried red dates) are other common ingredients.

In Korea there are there days in the lunar calendar, which mark the hottest and most sultry summer days in Korea: Chobok (초복), Jungbok (중복) and Malbok (말복)! And Koreans believe, that eating samgyetang on these days promotes health and stamina! As the Korean saying goes, eating the hot soup is in the Korean summer is like “fighting the heat with heat.” And I have to say, I immediately felt better after eating this delicious Korean Ginseng Chicken Soup aka SamGyeTang (삼계탕). I am already looking forward to also eat Samgyetang Jungbok (중복) and Malbok (말복), to complete my SamGyeTang „quest“ :D Haha!

Besides eating the delicious Korean Traditional Ginseng Chicken Soup Alex and me talked about loosing weight in Korea, why it is so hard to do and what the differences are to Austria and the USA. It is really hard to loose weight, since Korea has such a hughe drinking and eating culture. So if you are Korean, how do you keep in shape meanwhile eating all the delicious Korean food and drinking so much as well. Please let me know!

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to my 41th video of Mika in Korea. This time we went to visit my good friend Tomek and his wife in Yongin (용인), where they invited me to eat some local specialities: Gopchang-jeongol (곱창전골), or beef tripe hot pot and this is a spicy Korean stew or casserole made by boiling beef tripe, vegetables, and seasonings in beef broth. Basically beef intestines! There is also something similiar in Austrian and Polish culture but I was never into intestines. But this time I wanted to try something new, so we went to eat some Gopchang (곱창)! The first bites felt a little bit wired but with time I got used to it and I kinda enjoyed it. Tomek was really into it, it is one of his favorite Korean food.

Besides eating Gopchang-jeongol (곱창전골) we also talked about difficulties for foreigners living in South Korea. Of course withhout learning the language everything would be difficult for us but we tried to focus on topics, that a generel a little bit inconvenient for us foreigners. For example, my full name is too long for Korean system, so I can’t get a pointcard in the supermarket. Also finding Western style breakfast isn’t easy in Korea. Also it is difficult for taller people to live in Korea and to make friends with Korean people, if you don’t work in a Korean company. If you have something to add up, I am curious about your difficulties and experiences as a foreigner here in Korea. Please let me know them in the comments!

Kimchijjigae (김치찌개) is my favorite Korean food next to Dakgalbi, so I was really looking forward to try this local Kimchi Jjigae place. For the ones, who don’t know what Kimchi Jjigae is: Kimchi stew is one of the most-loved of all the stews in Korean cuisine. It’s a warm, hearty, spicy, savory, delicious dish that pretty much everyone loves. As long as they can handle spicy food, I never met a person who didn’t like kimchi-jjigae. Even Paul, who isn’t as good with spicy Korean food could enjoy this delicious Kimchi Jjigae!

Besides eating Kimchi Jjigae (김치찌개), we also talked about 5 things foreigners love about Korea. So we brought up topics like Korean food, that meals in Korea are way cheaper than abroad, that everything is quick here, so you don’t need to wait for anything, like for example for the internet setup. Also we talked about the ultimate convenience of living in South Korea and also the Korean medical care system. Of course there are many more things, foreigners like about living in Korea, but these are our 5 shorts points and insights.

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to my 36th video of Mika in Korea. And yeah, this time my good friend Cedric and I went to eat some delicious Dwaeji Gukbap, what is some kind of Korean Hangover Soup, after we had a very, very rough night celebrating our friend’s birthday party! Dwaeji Gukbap is a Pork and Rice Soup and is originally a specialty dish from Busan, which is relatively unknown and rare in Seoul, but we found a place in Hapjeong, where they served a really good Dwaeji Gukbap (돼지국밥). The special thing about Dwaeji Gukbap is, that it is a high maintenance recipe as it takes hours of boiling the pork bone to get the milk-coloured broth. Usually it is encouraged for women after childbirth and for the weak, or for people who went out all night long and came back home early in the morning kkkk. Like us! We also talked about Hangover drinks and food in the USA and in Austria and what differences there are. Also I found out, that the famous Austrian „Reparaturseidl“ also exists in South Korea, being called Haejangsul (해장술). But this time I didn’t drink anything, because my stomache could barely handle the food. We really enjoyed our Korean Hangover Soup Dwaeji Gukbap and we definitely felt immediately way better after finishing the Busan specialty dish!

We decided to eat some traditional Korean BBQ, more specifically skirt meat or skirt steak, called Galmaegisal. There is a really good place we both like in Sindorim, so we decided to go there. Of course we can’t just eat skirt steak without any booze or Korean alcohol, for Korean BBQ Soju is a must-have on the table! These days I am really a lot into Somek (소맥), some kind of beer cocktail made with soju and beer! I also practised my Soju Mixing in that video, thx for my Korean cousine for teaching me that :D Also we talk about, why foreigners like Korean BBQ so much and generally about different food cultures and etiquettes. We really had a lot of fun, unfortunately I drank a little bit too much Somek at the end, so I got a little tipsy and crazy at the end. 안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to the 33rd video of Mika in Korea. This time it was Children’s Day in Korea (어린이날) and we really had a great sunny weather on that day. So how about to meet up some friends and do a picknick in the Mangwon Hangang Park (망원 한강 공원)? Luckily my two close buddies Alex and Cedric (both Youtubers, please check out their channels) had some time on Children’s Day, so we met up in Hapjeong, bought some wine and ordered some chicken to enjoy it together in Mangwon Park (망원 공원). I know, usually it is chicken and beer, chimek, but since we all had chicken and beer a lot lately, we came up with the idea, to enjoy the chicken with some wine: Chiwa / 치와! We know it isn’t popular in Korea but in some funny way it worked. Of course it isn’t as good as chicken & beer (Chimaek / 치맥) but still we enjoy it together with wine. We really spent a nice time chatting about life, friendship and of course Youtube and stayed in the Mangwon Park until the evening. Thx Alex and Cedric for joining, let’s do this soon again!

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to my 30th vlog. And to our last video blog episode with my Austrian friend Susanne! For our last mukbang we went to eat some authentic Korean fried chicken and beer, something Korean love eat at drinking places. In Korea fried chicken and beer is called „chimek“ (치맥), what is the short cut for chicken & maekju (beer in Korean). Of course we just didn’t drink beer, we mixed the beer with some Soju, what is called Somek, the short cut of Soju and maekju! So somehow it was a Chi-so-mek experience for Susanne at the end of her stay in Seoul / South Korea. We got drunk really quick, so we really had a lot of fun this chicken place and you can see some nice reactions. Also Susanne was learning how to order chicken and beer in Korean, so this was also fun to watch.  If you want to also eat your chimek here, the place is called „여기가 만세닭“ and is located in Sindorim.

snippet.title: Poopooland / 놀이똥산 - A weird Amusement Park in South Korea (Mika in Korea Vlog #019)
snippet.description:
Subscribe Mika in Korea for more Videos http://www.kvlog.com

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to my 19th vlog. This time me and my friends went to a weird Amusement Park called PooPooLand (놀이똥산), where everything is around poop / poo poo! :D It is indeed such a weird place to be, because literally everywhere you can see Poop and shit everywhere. Of course not real one, but still. You start at the beginning with some information about Poop and digestion and then you can see (and feel) how the food is processed. At the end you need to slide down a slide, to be excremented. One of my weirdest experiences in Korea so far, haha! Also PooPooLand is playing with the Korean words, because „놀이동산“ means amusement park and they slightly changed into „놀이똥산“, where they put the „poo“ into the word of the amusement park. Anyway, if you are looking for a special adventure and you are into wired amusement parks, i can recommend you to visit PooPooLand :) We had a lot of fun and shot a lot of funny footage. And as always, if you like this video, please hit the thumbs up and also subscribe to my Youtube Channel, if you are interested about my life as a foreigner in South Korea :) Thx for watching and have a great day, cheers Mika!

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to my 17th vlog. Today Sunjin, Sujin and me went to the Lotte World Adventure (롯데월드 어드벤처) to have some fun and playing around a little bit. Lotte World Adventure is the largest indoor amusement park in the world, so if you are into Themeparks and you are in Seoul, South Korea, you definitely need to check out Lotte World (롯데월드). Altough we bough the Day-Pass, we couldn’t even do half of the attractions and roller coaster fun we planned to do. Most of the time there were huge waiting lines in front of every Roller Coaster, some even until one hour! Holy smokes! But we managed to get at least on one of the Roller Coaster in Lotte World and i was even allowed to film! Although they took away my camera at first, i got it back with the notice, that if the camera is damaged, it is my fault. And they were right, the Comet Express Roller Coaster (혜성특급) was sooo fast, that i really nearly lost my camera. Luckily nothing happened and i captured some funny moments during the ride. Unfortunately it was pretty dark during the ride, but you can hear us screaming well, haha! Lotte World is a fun Themepark to visit, so if you want to have some fun in Seoul, check it out. If you liked my video, please hit the Thumbs Up Button and also subscribe to my Youtube Channel, if you didn’t do so far. Did you also visit the Lotte World Adventure (롯데월드 어드벤처) Themepark? snippet.title: 설날 맞이 쿡방 🇰🇷 외국인들이 만든 떡국 맛은 어떨까요? 외국인 먹방 반응 (미카인코리아 064)
snippet.description:
더 많은 비디오를 원하시면 Mika in Korea를 구독 해 주세요 https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCehQUCosGefZu2xG_cqqLDA?sub_confirmation=1

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

안녕하세요, 여러분. 한국의 가장 큰 명절 중 하나인 설날이 돌아왔어요! 한국에는 새해에 떡국을 먹는 풍습이 있잖아요. 떡국을 먹어야 한 살을 더 먹는다고 하는데, 이번 영상에서는 한국식으로 설날을 보내기 위해서 떡국을 먹어보기로 했어요. 

라라랜드 (Laraland) 에서 온 라라와 함께 우리의 한국인 배우자들을 위해서 떡국 요리에 도전했는데요 저희가 만든 떡국은 "소고기 떡국" 입니다. 라라는 아예 한국 요리를 해 본 것 자체가 처음이었다고 해요. 저도 떡국은 처음 만들어봐서 긴장도 되고 실수도 많이 했지만 정말 재밌는 경험이었어요. 저희가 만든 떡국 맛이 어땠을지 궁금하시면 영상을 끝까지 봐주세요! 

제 아내 수진이와 라라의 남편 케니가 공정하게 떡국 맛을 평가 해주었구요, 결혼 후 한국에서 보내는 명절이 어떤지에 대해서도 짧게 이야기를 나누었습니다. 쿡방은 처음이었는데 어떠셨을지 모르겠어요. 재미있으셨다면 댓글 많이 남겨주세요!!

아직 제 채널을 구독하지 않으셨다면, 꼭 구독 해 주세요!! 한국에서의 제 일상을 구경하시고 응원 해 주세요.
제 비디오를 봐 주셔서 정말 감사합니다. 다음에 또 만나요. 안녕!

라라랜드 (Laraland) 에서 온 라라와 함께 우리의 한국인 배우자들을 위해서 떡국 요리에 도전했는데요 저희가 만든 떡국은 "소고기 떡국" 입니다. 라라는 아예 한국 요리를 해 본 것 자체가 처음이었다고 해요. 저도 떡국은 처음 만들어봐서 긴장도 되고 실수도 많이 했지만 정말 재밌는 경험이었어요. 저희가 만든 떡국 맛이 어땠을지 궁금하시면 영상을 끝까지 봐주세요! 

제 아내 수진이와 라라의 남편 케니가 공정하게 떡국 맛을 평가 해주었구요, 결혼 후 한국에서 보내는 명절이 어떤지에 대해서도 짧게 이야기를 나누었습니다. 쿡방은 처음이었는데 어떠셨을지 모르겠어요. 재미있으셨다면 댓글 많이 남겨주세요!!

아직 제 채널을 구독하지 않으셨다면, 꼭 구독 해 주세요!! 한국에서의 제 일상을 구경하시고 응원 해 주세요.

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to the 64th video of Mika in Korea. These days Korean people are celebrating Seollal (설날) (Korean New Year’s Day), which is the first day of the Lunar calendar and next to Chuseok (추석) one of the most important holidays in Korea. And on that day Koreans have a tradition, they are eating Tteokguk (떡국), a Korean Rice Cake Soup! According to Korean age reckoning, everyone’s age went up one year on Seollal, and the process wasn’t totally complete until you had a bowl of Tteokguk.

Since I am living in South Korea, I am also celebrating Seollal with my family. So for that occasion I thought it would be a great idea to cook this Korean Traditional dish and together with Lara from Laraland (라라랜드) we did some shopping together, bought all the ingredients for Tteokguk, checked a recipe online how to make Tteokguk and finally cooked it in Laras kitchen. For Lara it was the first time that she ever cooked a Korean dish. So if you want to know, if we succeeded and if our Western Style of Tteokguk tasted well, you have to watch this video :D My wife Sujin and Lara’s husband Kenny were the Korean judges and told us, if they liked our Tteokguk or not. It was super fun shooting with Lara and if you want to see more cooking videos, please let me know in the description.

As usually, if you didn’t subscribe to my Youtube channel yet, I would be super duper happy, if you would do so! Follow me on my adventures here as a foreigner living in South Korea. Again, thank you soooo much for watching, I truly appreciate. 다음에 또 만나요. 안녕!

en.description:

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - 

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to the 62nd video of Mika in Korea. Happy new year! I really hope, all you guys had a great start into the new year 2019! For my very first video of the year I invited my dear friends Alex and Cedric to enjoy some really spicy Korean rice cake, called tteokbokki (떡볶이) in Korean. Of course we suffered a lot because it was really spicy and we kinda made a mukbang eating challenge out of it. For those people, who doesn’t know what tteokbokki is: it is a highly popular Korean street food and a delicious comfort food! You can eat it on the street, in a restaurant of also easily make it by yourself at home. We ordered ours as a home delivery food.

Please also check out my friends videos, I mentioned in our video:
KOREA IS EPIC! TOP 7 Outdoor Adventures in South Korea! - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yw9yxEUKnZg

en.title: Schloß Schönbrunn Christmas Market 🇦🇹 Austrian Delicacies & Punch Mukbang (Mika in Korea 061)
en.description:
Subscribe Mika in Korea 🇦🇹 🇰🇷 for more Videos https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCehQUCosGefZu2xG_cqqLDA?sub_confirmation=1
and follow me on Instagram https://www.instagram.com/mikainkorea/
And follow Daldal.tv for some couple content: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCt4Dm5x9HODOUr-nbnlT_Ng?sub_confirmation=1

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - 

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to the 61st video of Mika in Korea. And I am back in Austria for Christmas and before heading home to my parents town I stayed in Vienna for 2 days to be able to visit one of the most beautiful Christmas Markets in Vienna: the Schloß Schönbrunn Christmas Market! Unfortunately the weather wasnt the best because it was rainy but thanks to my friends Susl and Alice I spend a really nice time at the Schloß Schönbrunn. Together we enjoyed various kinds of Punch (also called Glühwein / Mulled wine) and ate a lot of Austrian Delicacies, which we call „Schmankerl“ in Austrian. We tried Käsenockerl (or Käsespätzle), Ofen Kartoffel (baked potato) and for dessert Kaiserschmarrn mit Zwetschkenröster (Sugared pancake with stewed plums), which is really super popular in Austria. I really hope you ll enjoy my Austrian Christmas Edition of a „Mukbang“ video. If you have any question regarding one of the Austrian dishes, please let me know in the comments.

As usually, if you didn’t subscribe to my Youtube channel yet, I would be super duper happy, if you would do so! Follow me on my adventures here as a foreigner living in South Korea. Again, thank you soooo much for watching, I truly appreciate. 다음에 또 만나요. 안녕!

안녕하세요, 여러분. 미카인코리아의 60번째 비디오를 봐주셔서 감사합니다. 오늘 영상에서는 "돔앤효"의 도미닉을 만나 뜨끈한 겨울 음식을 먹으러 갔어요. 한국에 있는 유튜버들끼리 크리스마스 파티를 하기로 한 날이었는데, 파티에 가기 전에 뭔가 따뜻한 음식을 먹고 가고 싶었어요. 순댓국은 제 친구 도미닉이 가장 좋아하는 한국 음식 중 하나라서 순댓국을 먹어보기로 했답니다.

주말 오후 홍대에서 촬영을 하려다보니 자리가 있는 식당을 찾는 것부터가 만만치 않더라구요. 세 번째로 간 식당에 다행이 자리도 있고 촬영도 허락 해 주셔서 영상을 찍을 수 있었답니다. 식당이 조금 어두워서 영상이 깨끗하게 나오진 않았지만 그래도 재미있게 봐주세요!!

저는 여태 돼지국밥은 많이 먹어봤는데 순댓국은 한 번도 안 먹어봤었거든요. 제가 순댓국을 좋아했을까요? 궁금하신 분들은 영상을 끝까지 봐주세요!

순댓국을 먹으면서 외국인으로서 한국에서 크리스마스를 보내는 것이 어떤지에 대해서 짧은 대화도 나눴어요. 저는 크리스마스 때마다 오스트리아에 가서 가족들과 크리스마스를 보내고 오는데요, 올 해도 오스트리아로 곧 떠날 거랍니다. 오스트리아에서 보고 싶은 것들이나 궁금한 점들이 있으시면 댓글로 알려주세요. 그리고 여러분들은 크리스마스를 어떻게 보내시는 지도 알려주세요.

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

안녕하세요, 여러분. 미카인코리아의 60번째 비디오를 봐주셔서 감사합니다. 오늘 영상에서는 "돔앤효"의 도미닉을 만나 뜨끈한 겨울 음식을 먹으러 갔어요. 한국에 있는 유튜버들끼리 크리스마스 파티를 하기로 한 날이었는데, 파티에 가기 전에 뭔가 따뜻한 음식을 먹고 가고 싶었어요. 순댓국은 제 친구 도미닉이 가장 좋아하는 한국 음식 중 하나라서 순댓국을 먹어보기로 했답니다.

주말 오후 홍대에서 촬영을 하려다보니 자리가 있는 식당을 찾는 것부터가 만만치 않더라구요. 세 번째로 간 식당에 다행이 자리도 있고 촬영도 허락 해 주셔서 영상을 찍을 수 있었답니다. 식당이 조금 어두워서 영상이 깨끗하게 나오진 않았지만 그래도 재미있게 봐주세요!!

저는 여태 돼지국밥은 많이 먹어봤는데 순댓국은 한 번도 안 먹어봤었거든요. 제가 순댓국을 좋아했을까요? 궁금하신 분들은 영상을 끝까지 봐주세요!

순댓국을 먹으면서 외국인으로서 한국에서 크리스마스를 보내는 것이 어떤지에 대해서 짧은 대화도 나눴어요. 저는 크리스마스 때마다 오스트리아에 가서 가족들과 크리스마스를 보내고 오는데요, 올 해도 오스트리아로 곧 떠날 거랍니다. 오스트리아에서 보고 싶은 것들이나 궁금한 점들이 있으시면 댓글로 알려주세요. 그리고 여러분들은 크리스마스를 어떻게 보내시는 지도 알려주세요.

아직 제 채널을 구독하지 않으셨다면, 꼭 구독 해 주세요!! 한국에서의 제 일상을 구경하시고 응원 해 주세요.
제 비디오를 봐 주셔서 정말 감사합니다. 다음에 또 만나요. 안녕!

en.title: Mika eats Blood Sausage Soup for the first time 🇰🇷 Korean Sundaeguk Mukbang (Mika in Korea 060)
en.description:
Subscribe Mika in Korea 🇦🇹 🇰🇷 for more Videos https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCehQUCosGefZu2xG_cqqLDA?sub_confirmation=1
and follow me on Instagram https://www.instagram.com/mikainkorea/
And follow Daldal.tv for some couple content: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCt4Dm5x9HODOUr-nbnlT_Ng?sub_confirmation=1

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - 

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to the 60th video of Mika in Korea. And this time Youtuber Dominik from Dom & Hyo joins me again for some delicious Korean food. And because it is really cold these days and we were heading to the Youtubers in Korea Christmas Party, we decided to put something warm into our bellies and eat one of Dom’s favorite Korean dishes: Blood Sausage Soup or also called Sundaeguk (순댓국). It wasn’t easy to find a restaurant in Hongdae on a saturday afternoon, which had a place for us but luckily the third restaurant had some space for us. Unfortunately it was a little bit dark, sorry for the not sooo great footage this time. For Mika it was the first time eating Blood Sausage Soup, so if you are curious, how he liked the dish, please watch the video.

Also we talked about how to celebrate Christmas in Korea as a foreigner. Mika is going back to Austria to celebrate Christmas with his family, so if you want him to show you something from Austria, please let him know in the comments! And also curious, how you guys are celebrating Christmas in Korea. Let me know!

As usually, if you didn’t subscribe to my Youtube channel yet, I would be super duper happy, if you would do so! Follow me on my adventures here as a foreigner living in South Korea. Again, thank you soooo much for watching, I truly appreciate. 다음에 또 만나요. 안녕!

snippet.description:
더 많은 비디오를 원하시면 Mika in Korea를 구독 해 주세요 https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCehQUCosGefZu2xG_cqqLDA?sub_confirmation=1
그리고 인스타그램에서 Mika in Korea를 팔로우 해 주세요 http://www.instagram.com/mikainkorea
저희 부부에 대해서 궁금하시면 달달티비를 구독 해 주세요 https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCt4Dm5x9HODOUr-nbnlT_Ng?sub_confirmation=1

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

안녕하세요, 여러분. 미카인코리아의 59번째 비디오를 봐주셔서 감사합니다. 11월과 12월은 김장철이죠? 한 번도 김치 만드는 걸 본 적이 없는 저를 위해 장모님께서 김장에 초대 해주셨어요. 부산은 날씨가 조금 더 따뜻해서 지금이 딱 김장철이거든요. 지난 주말에 촬영한 따끈따끈한 영상이에요!

장모님께서 하루 전에 배추도 절여 놓으시고, 양념도 준비 해 두셔서 저는 돕기만 하면 됐어요. 아침에 일어나서 절인 배추를 물에 씻어 물기를 빼고, 점심 때는 온갖 양념이 들어간 김장 양념에 배추를 버무리는 일을 했어요. 30포기를 담궜는데 정말 일이 많더라구요. (장모님, 존경합니다!) 힘들긴 했지만 정말 새로운 경험이었고, 사랑스러운 장모님과 정말 행복한 시간을 보냈어요.

저녁에는 돼지고기 수육과 갓 담근 김치를 먹었는데요, 장인어른께서 주시는 소주가 쓰지 않고 달더라구요. 정말 끝내주는 경험이었어요! 내년에도 꼭 김장하실 때 가서 도와 드릴 거에요.

아직 제 채널을 구독하지 않으셨다면, 꼭 구독 해 주세요!! 한국에서의 제 일상을 구경하시고 응원 해 주세요.
제 비디오를 봐 주셔서 정말 감사합니다. 다음에 또 만나요. 안녕!

en.description:
Subscribe Mika in Korea 🇦🇹 🇰🇷 for more Videos https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCehQUCosGefZu2xG_cqqLDA?sub_confirmation=1
and follow me on Instagram https://www.instagram.com/mikainkorea/
And follow Daldal.tv for some couple content: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCt4Dm5x9HODOUr-nbnlT_Ng?sub_confirmation=1

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - 

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to the 59th video of Mika in Korea. So November / Dezember is Kimjang season: the time to make cabbage kimchi! And because I never made Kimchi by myself and I always wanted to know, how to make Kimchi, I went to Busan to visit my lovely mom-in-law and help her with the Kimchi preparation, called Kimjang (김장). First we needed to wash the cabbage outside and bring it home, where we mixed it with all the ingredients. In total we made 30 cabbages into Kimchi, which was indeed a lot of work to do so. But for me it was a nice experience, making Kimjang for the first time and helping my mother-in-law. I had a great time with her but I definitely need to study more Korean to be able to talk to her more. And one thing is for sure: next year I will also come back to Busan for the Kimjang season and help my mom-in-law making Kimchi.

As usually, if you didn’t subscribe to my Youtube channel yet, I would be super duper happy, if you would do so! Follow me on my adventures here as a foreigner living in South Korea. Again, thank you soooo much for watching, I truly appreciate. 다음에 또 만나요. 안녕!

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

안녕하세요, 여러분. 미카인코리아의 59번째 비디오를 봐주셔서 감사합니다. 11월과 12월은 김장철이죠? 한 번도 김치 만드는 걸 본 적이 없는 저를 위해 장모님께서 김장에 초대 해주셨어요. 부산은 날씨가 조금 더 따뜻해서 지금이 딱 김장철이거든요. 지난 주말에 촬영한 따끈따끈한 영상이에요!

장모님께서 하루 전에 배추도 절여 놓으시고, 양념도 준비 해 두셔서 저는 돕기만 하면 됐어요. 아침에 일어나서 절인 배추를 물에 씻어 물기를 빼고, 점심 때는 온갖 양념이 들어간 김장 양념에 배추를 버무리는 일을 했어요. 30포기를 담궜는데 정말 일이 많더라구요. (장모님, 존경합니다!) 힘들긴 했지만 정말 새로운 경험이었고, 사랑스러운 장모님과 정말 행복한 시간을 보냈어요.

저녁에는 돼지고기 수육과 갓 담근 김치를 먹었는데요, 장인어른께서 주시는 소주가 쓰지 않고 달더라구요. 정말 끝내주는 경험이었어요! 내년에도 꼭 김장하실 때 가서 도와 드릴 거에요.

아직 제 채널을 구독하지 않으셨다면, 꼭 구독 해 주세요!! 한국에서의 제 일상을 구경하시고 응원 해 주세요.
제 비디오를 봐 주셔서 정말 감사합니다. 다음에 또 만나요. 안녕!

en.title: Popular Korean Street Food in Winter 🇰🇷 Tteokbokki, Sundae & Hotteok Mukbang (Mika in Korea 058)
en.description:
Subscribe Mika in Korea 🇦🇹 🇰🇷 for more Videos https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCehQUCosGefZu2xG_cqqLDA?sub_confirmation=1
and follow me on Instagram https://www.instagram.com/mikainkorea/
And follow Daldal.tv for some couple content: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCt4Dm5x9HODOUr-nbnlT_Ng?sub_confirmation=1

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - 

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to the 58th video of Mika in Korea. It is seriously getting cold here in Korea there days. The perfect time to enjoy some Popular Korean Street Food in Winter, called 길거리음식 in Korean! So i invited Cassie Casper (캐시 캐스퍼) to join me on a little Street Food Tour through the Mangwon Market (망원시장) in Seoul. Many of you will recognize Cassy from the popular Korean Learning Site „Talk to me in Korean“ or in short „ttmik“. Cassy is living in Korea already since over 8 years, so she was really able to give me a proper introduction into Korean food culture, explained me a lot of little things and taught me also Korean expressions. We tried various kinds of Korean street snacks, like Tteokbokki (떡볶이), Sundae (순대), Hotteok (호떡) and many more. Unfortunately we got full pretty fast, so I think, Cassy and I will meet up for a 2nd round of Korean Street Snacks, if you guys want to see us eating more. Let us know in the comment section!

As usually, if you didn’t subscribe to my Youtube channel yet, I would be super duper happy, if you would do so! Follow me on my adventures here as a foreigner living in South Korea. Again, thank you soooo much for watching, I truly appreciate. 다음에 또 만나요. 안녕!

en.title: Difference Between Korean & Western Humor? 🇰🇷 Korean Dumpling Hot Pot Mukbang (Mika in Korea 057)
en.description:
Subscribe Mika in Korea 🇦🇹 🇰🇷 for more Videos https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCehQUCosGefZu2xG_cqqLDA?sub_confirmation=1
and follow me on Instagram https://www.instagram.com/mikainkorea/

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - 

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to the 57th video of Mika in Korea. Winter finally arrived in Seoul / South Korea and it got really cold here. So instead of eating some Chimaek (Korean fried chicken) with beer, Paul and I decided to eat some healthy and warm dumpling hot pot (만두전골) with some homemade dumpling (손만두). Since Paul (aka Paul Seoul / 폴서울) is doing Stand-Up Comedy (스탠드업코미디) in Korean, we talked a little bit about humor in Korea and how Korean Humor and comedy is different from the humor in western countries. Please let me know in the comments, what you think about this topic and if you could tell me some funny Korean Comedy Shows, I would also highly appreciate.

As usually, if you didn’t subscribe to my Youtube channel yet, I would be super duper happy, if you would do so! Follow me on my adventures here as a foreigner living in South Korea. Again, thank you soooo much for watching, I truly appreciate. 다음에 또 만나요. 안녕!

안녕하세요, 여러분. 미카인코리아의 55번째 비디오를 봐주셔서 감사합니다. 오늘은 제 친한친구 미국친구 미친 알렉스와 함께 오리 주물럭을 먹으러 갔어요. 오스트리아에서 오리고기를 먹은 기억이 없어서 어머니께 여쭤봤더니 제가 어릴 때 크리스마스에 요리를 해 주셨다고 하네요. 그런데 기억이 나지는 않아요. ㅋㅋㅋ 한국식 오리 요리는 어떤지 알아보기 위해서 알렉스와 합정역 근처에 위치한 오리 식당을 찾았습니다.

en.title: Is Marinated Grilled Duck better than Dakgalbi? 🇰🇷 Korean Stir Fry Duck Mukbang (Mika in Korea 055)
en.description:
Subscribe Mika in Korea 🇦🇹 🇰🇷 for more Videos https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCehQUCosGefZu2xG_cqqLDA?sub_confirmation=1
and follow me on Instagram https://www.instagram.com/mikainkorea/

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - 

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to the 55th video of Mika in Korea. And in this video my good old friend 미국친구 Michin Alex joins me again for a delicious Korean Stir Fry Duck Mukbang, a Marinated Grilled Duck called 오리주물럭 in Korean. Since it’s been a long time I ate duck (오리고기) meat for the last time (I even don’t remember it anymore but my mom told me, she used to do it sometimes to christmas, when I was a child) I thought it would be a great opportunity to try out some Korean duck dish and went to a Korean Restaurant in Hapjeong with Alex. After enjoying the Korean Stir Fry Duck and comparing it to the delicious Dak-Galbi (Korean Spicy Chicken Stir Fry / 닭갈비) we finished the dish with some Fried Rice as a final Bokkeumbap (볶음밥). Of course it wouldn’t be a Mika in Korea episode without some Korean alcohol and day drinking as well. So we ordered some Bokbunjaju (복분자주), so called bokbunja wine, a Korean fruit wine made from wild Korean black raspberry. Needless to say we underestimated the alcohol percentage of the Bokbunjaju (복분자주), so we got a little bit drunk at the end. It was really a fun shooting with Alex and we enjoyed the Korean Stir Fry Duck a lot and talked about a few things as well.

Check out Alex' his video as well:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cWQysoCAbkU

As usually, if you didn’t subscribe to my Youtube channel yet, I would be super duper happy, if you would do so! Follow me on my adventures here as a foreigner living in South Korea. Again, thank you soooo much for watching, I truly appreciate. 다음에 또 만나요. 안녕!

en.title: Austrians 🇦🇹 climbing the Mt. Bukhansan / Baegundae Peak 🇰🇷 Kimbap Mukbang (Mika in Korea 054)
en.description:
Subscribe Mika in Korea 🇦🇹 🇰🇷 for more Videos https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCehQUCosGefZu2xG_cqqLDA?sub_confirmation=1
and follow me on Instagram https://www.instagram.com/mikainkorea/
And follow Daldal.tv for some couple content: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCt4Dm5x9HODOUr-nbnlT_Ng?sub_confirmation=1

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - 

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to the 54th video of Mika in Korea. After a crazy visit of the Gwangjang Market (광장시장) last week and eating the live Octopus (낙지) we decided to enjoy the nature in South Korea and climb the Mt. Bukhansan (북한산) / Baegundae Peak (백운대) in the Bukhansan National Park (북한산국립공원)! The weather was perfect for hiking and it was also beautiful to enjoy the nature in the middle of autumn. The hike itself was pretty exhausting, some of us were in a good shape and climbed up very quickly, the others were in not such a good shape and needed more time to conquer the Baegundae Peak (백운대). It took us nearly 2 hours to get to the peak but I can really say, it was worth the hike. The view above Seoul was really beautiful, unfortunately we didn’t shoot more footage on the very top since most of us where scared of heights. As a reward for reaching at the top of the Bukhansan I gave my Austrian friends some Korean Kimbap, which they enjoyed a lot. After this hike I needed to rest for three days but it was really worth the hike.

As usually, if you didn’t subscribe to my Youtube channel yet, I would be super duper happy, if you would do so! Follow me on my adventures here as a foreigner living in South Korea. Again, thank you soooo much for watching, I truly appreciate. 다음에 또 만나요. 안녕!

en.title: Korean Live Octopus Mukbang 🇰🇷 Foreigners visiting Gwangjang Market (Mika in Korea 053)
en.description:
Subscribe Mika in Korea 🇦🇹 🇰🇷 for more Videos https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCehQUCosGefZu2xG_cqqLDA?sub_confirmation=1
and follow me on Instagram https://www.instagram.com/mikainkorea/
And follow Daldal.tv for some couple content: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCt4Dm5x9HODOUr-nbnlT_Ng?sub_confirmation=1

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - 

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to the 53rd video of Mika in Korea.  And this time my good old friend Kriesi from Austria stopped by and also brought along his friends for a few days here in Seoul, South Korea. Of course I showed them around Seoul and one of the places they liked the most was the Gwangjang Market (광장시장). There we spend a lot of time exploring the market and trying out various kinds of Traditional Korean Food. Of course we stopped by the famous Bindae-tteok (빈대떡) place, where we ate quite a lot and also drink some makgeolli (막걸리). The guys stopped nearly at every food stand in the Gwangjang Market, so we also tried a small alive Octopus (낙지), Sundae (순대), Fish Bread (붕어빵), Gogi Mandu (고기만두), Kimchi Mandu (김치만두) and also enjoyed some Korean beer as well. At the end the guys did also some shopping for their friend. It was really fun shooting with the fellas and I really hope you will enjoy this Gwangjang Market Mukbang Food Tour as much as I need. Come one, I even tried some Octopus (낙지), if this isn’t worth checking out our today’s video, I don’t know what is kkkk.

As usually, if you didn’t subscribe to my Youtube channel yet, I would be super duper happy, if you would do so! Follow me on my adventures here as a foreigner living in South Korea. Again, thank you soooo much for watching, I truly appreciate. 다음에 또 만나요. 안녕!

We went to a Korean Restaurant in Hapjeong, which offered a vegetarian menu and we both decided to eat some healthy Bibimbab without meat! A Vegetarian Bibimbab, so to say. Of course we ordered some Makgeolli (막걸리) as well and we talked about healthy food, being a Vegetarian in Korea and we are also looking for some Korean Vegetarian Restaurants with good food, so if you know a good place in Seoul, please let me know in the comments. en.title: Enjoying some good Samgyeopsal (삼겹살) 🇰🇷 Korean BBQ Mukbang (Mika in Korea 051)
en.description:
Subscribe Mika in Korea 🇦🇹 🇰🇷 for more Videos https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCehQUCosGefZu2xG_cqqLDA?sub_confirmation=1
and follow me on Instagram https://www.instagram.com/mikainkorea/
And follow Daldal.tv for some couple content: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCt4Dm5x9HODOUr-nbnlT_Ng?sub_confirmation=1

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - 

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to the 51st video of Mika in Korea. And I am finally back in South Korea! Whoop, Whoop! Long time no see! I really missed Korean food, so I am happy I can restart my Korean Mukang (먹방) Series. And together with my good old friend Cedric (Skycedi) we went to eat some delicious Samgyeopsal (삼겹살) in Hapjeong, some random Korean BBQ restaurant we bumped into. Of course we also had some Somek (소맥), Korean Beer (맥주) and Soju (소주), but we didn’t drink too much this time, since we were both heading to an event afterwards. Meanwhile eating some delicious Samgyeopsal (삼겹살) and Galmaegisal (갈매기살) we also talked about things, I missed about Korea and also if South Korea feels like home to me or not. So if you are curious how we foreigners feel about living here in South Korea, please watch the video until the end.

As usually, if you didn’t subscribe to my Youtube channel yet, I would be super duper happy, if you would do so! Follow me on my adventures here as a foreigner living in South Korea. Again, thank you soooo much for watching, I truly appreciate. 다음에 또 만나요. 안녕!

en.title: Foreigners 🇦🇹 eating Korean 🇰🇷 Ramyeon for the first time (Mika in Korea 050)
en.description:
Subscribe Mika in Korea 🇦🇹 🇰🇷 for more Videos https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCehQUCosGefZu2xG_cqqLDA?sub_confirmation=1
and follow me on Instagram https://www.instagram.com/mikainkorea/
And follow Daldal.tv for some couple content: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCt4Dm5x9HODOUr-nbnlT_Ng?sub_confirmation=1

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - 

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to the 50th video of Mika in Korea. On my very last day of my stay in Austria I introduced Korean Ramyeon to my Austrian friends. They never ate Korean Ramyeon before, so it was really the first time for them trying Korean Instant Noodles. I brought 3 different kind of Ramyeon along, one Jjawang Ramyeon (짜왕), the popular Shin Ramyeon (신라면) and the notorious hot Buldak-Bokkeum-Myeon (불닭볶음면), the most spicy Ramyeon in Korea. I let my friends try out all the different Korean Cup Noodles / Instant Noodles and if you want to know, which one they liked the most, you have to watch the video until the very end. I really hope my friends will come and visit me in South Korea very soon, so we can eat some more delicious Korean food instead of ready-to-cook Instant Noodles / Ramyeon.

As usually, if you didn’t subscribe to my Youtube channel yet, I would be super duper happy, if you would do so! Follow me on my adventures here as a foreigner living in South Korea. Again, thank you soooo much for watching, I truly appreciate. 다음에 또 만나요. 안녕!

And for the wedding of my dear friends Dani & Martin I was even shooting some videos, so I can show it to you in my Youtube channel. Since I was the best man for Martin, I was organizing the Bachelor Party together with Christof, Martin’s 2nd best man! In Austria we call this „Junggesellenabschied“, it is usually the last evening in „freedom“ for the groom, also for the bride, who is celebrating the same with the bridesmaids. For our manly Bachelor Party we went to Tirol to the Area 47, where we spent the full weekend doing fun outdoor activities and having a great party. Of course I can’t show you all the juicy and naughty stuff we did at the evening but I can assure you it was a wild party at the end.

For the wedding Dani and Martin decided to get married in Montenegro, in Herceg Novi. The wedding was held in some kind of vineyard / winery with a breath-talking view. Then we went down through the city, accompanied by a Montenegri Gispy band. At the end we entered a boat and celebrated the wedding-after-party on the sea! Super beautiful and really an awesome wedding. The best, I ever attended and hard to beat for future wedding celebrations.

I hope you’ll enjoy my vlog from Europe, showing you how Western people are celebrating the bachelor party and wedding. Hopefully Dani & Martin will visit me soon again in South Korea as well :)

ko.title: 오스트리아 🇦🇹 사나이들이 총각파티를 즐기는 법! 🎉 (미카인코리아 049)
ko.description:
더 많은 비디오를 원하시면 Mika in Korea를 구독 해 주세요 https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCehQUCosGefZu2xG_cqqLDA?sub_confirmation=1
그리고 인스타그램에서 Mika in Korea를 팔로우 해 주세요 http://www.instagram.com/mikainkorea
저희 부부에 대해서 궁금하시면 달달티비를 구독 해 주세요 https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCt4Dm5x9HODOUr-nbnlT_Ng?sub_confirmation=1

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

안녕하세요, 여러분! 미카인코리아의 49번째 브이로그를 봐주셔서 감사합니다. 오스트리아에 다녀오느라 9월에 영상을 올리지 못했어요!! ㅜ 혹시 기다리셨다면 정말 죄송해요! 다시 열심히 할 예정이니 앞으로도 많이 봐주세요! 

친한 친구들의 결혼식이 2개나 있었고, 가족들도 보고 싶어서 오스트리아에 한달간 다녀왔어요. 제 소중한 친구 다니와 마틴의 결혼식에서 저는 마틴의 베스트맨 (신랑들러리) 이기도했는데요, 그래서 마틴을 위한 총각파티를 준비했답니다. 오스트리아에서는 총각파티를 „Junggesellenabschied“ 라고 부르는데요, 신랑에겐 "마지막 자유의 날"이라 더 특별한 것 같아요. 

"남자다운" 총각파티를 위해서 친구들과 티롤의 아레아 47이란 곳에 갔는데요, 여러가지 야외 액티비티와 멋진 파티를 할 수 있는 곳이었어요. 물론 프라이버시와 유튜브 심의상 보여드리지 못한 부분이 더 많이 있지만 (웃음) 그래도 정말 재미있는 시간이었으니 여러분들도 영상을 보시면서 함께 그 재미를 느끼실 수 있길 바래요!!

마지막엔 다니와 마틴의 아름다운 결혼식 영상도 포함되어 있는데요, 오스트리아가아니라 지중해의 아름다운 섬, 몬테네그로에서 결혼식을 올렸답니다. 아름다운 포도밭에서 결혼식을 올렸는데요, 멋진 풍경이니 꼭 구경해보세요! 결혼식이 끝난 후에는 발칸반도 (결혼식) 정통이기도 한 집시 밴드들도 초대해서 음악을 연주하면서 시내 곳곳을 걸어다녔어요. 신나고, 개인적으로도 의미있는 영상이니 여러분들도 행복한 마음으로 봐주시고 예쁜 댓글 많이 남겨주시면 감사하겠습니다!

오늘도 제 브이로그를 봐주신 모든 분들 너무 감사드리구요, 다니랑 마틴이 곧 한국에 놀러와서 여러가지 체험을 같이 해 볼 수 있다면 너무 좋을 것 같아요. 제 친구 다니와 마틴의 행복한 결혼생활을 위해서 응원의 메세지 많이 남겨주세요! 🙂

아직 제 채널을 구독하지 않으셨다면, 꼭 구독 해 주세요!! 한국에서의 제 일상을 구경하시고 응원 해 주세요.
제 비디오를 봐 주셔서 정말 감사합니다. 다음에 또 만나요. 안녕!

snippet.title: Korean Fried Food Mukbang 🇰🇷 Modeum-Jeon Made Dish & Makgeolli (Mika in Korea 048)
snippet.description:
Subscribe Mika in Korea 🇦🇹 🇰🇷 for more Videos https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCehQUCosGefZu2xG_cqqLDA?sub_confirmation=1
and follow me on Instagram https://www.instagram.com/mikainkorea/
And follow Daldal.tv for some couple content: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCt4Dm5x9HODOUr-nbnlT_Ng?sub_confirmation=1

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - 

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to the 48th video of Mika in Korea. It is still hot in Seoul and Mika suggest to fight the heat with drinking some makgeolli (막걸리) and eating some assorted jeon / modeumjeon made dish (모듬전) in a local makgeolli bar in Sindorim. Usually you eat that kind of food and drink makgeolli when it rains but Mika couldn’t wait anymore and really wanted to eat this kind of delicious Korean Anju food! And in this video his French friend Sebastian / Seboom joined him for this weeks mukbang / sulbang video :D

The modeum-jeon (모듬전) contained a hugh variations of different jeons. fish jeon (생선전), meat jeon (고기전), zucchini jeon (애호박전), tofu jeon (두부전), mushroom jeon (버섯전), perilla leaf jeon (깻잎전) and autumn squash jeon (단호박전). And they all were extremely delicious!

Besides eating the Korean modeum-jeon (모듬전) and enjyoing two bottles of Makgeolli we also talked shortly about foreigners being lonely in South Korea, sharing own experiences. It isn’t easy for foreigners living in Korea and they feel lonely many times. 

Mika and Sebastian had a lot of fun shooting this kind of video and enjoyed this kind of Korean fried food a lot. Next time they will eat it again when it is finally rainy in Seoul!

As usually, if you didn’t subscribe to my Youtube channel yet, I would be super duper happy, if you would do so! Follow me on my adventures here as a foreigner living in South Korea. Again, thank you soooo much for watching, I truly appreciate. 다음에 또 만나요. 안녕!

snippet.title: Dwaeji Galbi Korean Mukbang 🤗 Friendship in Korea & Western countries (Mika in Korea 047)
snippet.description:
Subscribe Mika in Korea 🇦🇹 🇰🇷 for more Videos https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCehQUCosGefZu2xG_cqqLDA?sub_confirmation=1
and follow me on Instagram https://www.instagram.com/mikainkorea/
And follow Daldal.tv for some couple content: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCt4Dm5x9HODOUr-nbnlT_Ng?sub_confirmation=1

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - 

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to my 47th video of Mika in Korea. And today my dear friend Sharoon joins me once again to eat some delicious Korean food and talk a little bit about our lives as foreigners here in Korea. This time we followed one of our viewers recommendation and went to a famous Dwaeji Galbi Restaurant, where we enjoyed some really delicious Korean BBQ. For those who doesn’t know what Dwaeji Galbi (돼지갈비) is, this is grilled pork ribs with a marinated sauce. Of course we had a small chitchat, this time we talked about friendship in Korea & Western countries and the differences in both cultures. So we talked about the way of friendship in Korea, why age gap matters here and why it doesn’t in western culture but also the spicy topic, if men and women can be friends in general. What do you think? Can men and women be friends? Is it different in Korea. Please let me know in the comment section what you think about this. Also I would highly appreciate your opinion about friendship and what you think, is different between a Korean and a western friendship.

As usually, if you didn’t subscribe to my Youtube channel yet, I would be super duper happy, if you would do so! Follow me on my adventures here as a foreigner living in South Korea. Again, thank you soooo much for watching, I truly appreciate. 다음에 또 만나요. 안녕!

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to my 46th video of Mika in Korea. And today I am with Ding Ding 딩딩 and Cathy 캐시 from 빨간맛. And those two crazy Korean Girls introduced me to some Girlish Korean DIY Convenience Store Cocktails. So we were mixing different kinds of Korean alcohol, soft drinks and ice from the Convenience store to some hopefully tasty and cheap Convenience Store Cocktails. Of course if you start to drink different kinds of cocktails and to mix different kind of alcohol, you get drunk really, really fast. We also ordered some Jokbal as a sidedish, which was really, really good. We really want to do more Korean DIY Convenience Store Drinking videos, so after this Girlish Cocktails I really want to do a video with some guys, introducing me „manly“ Korean DIY Convenience Store drinks.

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to my 45th video of Mika in Korea. And this time I am answering all you guys questions, that you ask me in the last episodes, especially in the last one. Thank you soooo much for all the questions, I truly appreciate! Some of the Questions are: Am I an actor in Korea? Am I a really Suljengi? What is my favorite Korean food? My Biggest cultural shock? Difference between German and Austrian Language? What are some difficult German words? And many more. If you liked that episodes, please let me know, so I will do another one in the near future :)

Besides answering all the questions I was enjoying some Korean Jjimdak, a Korean Braised Chicken. It is made with chicken, various vegetables marinated in a ganjang (Korean soy sauce) based sauce. Super delicious. And it isn’t just a regular Jjimdak, no, it is a with love home-made Jjimdak from my lovely wife Sujin. Thank you soooo much for cooking, it was really yummy!


저는 한국에서 배우일까요?
저는 정말 술쟁이일까요?

한국에 와서 겪은 가장 큰 문화 충격은요?
독일과 오스트리아에서 쓰는 독일어의 차이점은 뭘까요?
발음하기 힘든 독일어 단어들?!

ko.title: 제가 배우냐구요? 😎 무엇이든 물어보세요! 찜닭과 함께하는 Q&A (미카인코리아 045)
ko.description:
더 많은 비디오를 원하시면 Mika in Korea를 구독 해 주세요 https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCehQUCosGefZu2xG_cqqLDA?sub_confirmation=1

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

안녕하세요, 여러분. 미카인코리아의 45번째 비디오를 봐주셔서 감사합니다. 지난번 비디오에서 제게 궁금한 것이 있으시면 질문 해 달라고 요청드렸었는데요, 다행히 많은 분들이 질문을 주셔서 비디오로 만들어 봤습니다. 질문 주신 분들 정말 감사드려요!!! 받았던 질문 중에 몇 가지만 미리 알려드리자면, 제가 배우가 되고 싶은지, 저는 정말 술쟁이인지, 제일 좋아하는 한국 음식은 무엇인지, 가장 큰 문화충격은 무엇이었는지, 독일과 오스트리아에서 쓰는 독일어의 차이점은 무엇인지 등등이 있었답니다. 

저를 이미 알고 계시는 분들도 잘 모르시는 분들도 모두 재미있게 봐 주셨으면 좋겠습니다. 앞으로도 제 비디오를 봐주시는 여러분들과 많이 소통하고 싶어요. 늘 감사합니다. 🙂 

질문에 대답하는 거 말고도 이번 비디오에서는 아내가 직접 요리해 준 찜닭을 먹었는데요, 제가 너무 좋아해서 아내한테 늘 해 달라고 한답니다. 아내가 할 줄 아니까 밖에서 먹는 것 보다 집에서 먹는 게 더 맛있어요!! 요리 해 준 나의 아내, 수진, 고마워요!!

아직 제 채널을 구독하지 않으셨다면, 꼭 구독 해 주세요!! 한국에서의 제 일상을 구경하시고 응원 해 주세요.
제 비디오를 봐 주셔서 정말 감사합니다. 다음에 또 만나요. 안녕!

snippet.title: Korean Tongue Twisters & Why Korean language is difficult 😝 Budaejjigae Mukbang (Mika in Korea 044)
snippet.description:
Subscribe Mika in Korea 🇦🇹 🇰🇷 for more Videos https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCehQUCosGefZu2xG_cqqLDA?sub_confirmation=1

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - 

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to my 44th video of Mika in Korea. This time my old friend Stu joins me for a Budaejjigae Mukbang and we are talking about Korean language, why it is difficult for foreigners to learn and also trying to learn some Korean Tongue Twisters. Which was really funny for everybody who listened to us in the restaurant. Stu is originally from London / England and he moved to Korea two years ago to get live with his Korean wife. We met in the Language Course, where we both studies Korean for one year together. Stu studied Korean pretty well lately, unfortunately I didn’t have so much time to practise / study Korean but I promise I ll get to it very soon again!

Although it was really hot outside we enjoyed the Budaejjigae a lot. Also drinking 1-2 shots of Soju, what else :D We really hope you had fun listening to our versions of the Korean Tongue Twisters. Perhaps you are interested in some funny German words and Tongue Twisters as well? Please let me know in the comment section! kkkkk

As usually, if you didn’t subscribe to my Youtube channel yet, I would be super duper happy, if you would do so! Follow me on my adventures here as a foreigner living in South Korea. Again, thank you soooo much for watching, I truly appreciate. 다음에 또 만나요. 안녕!

안녕하세요, 여러분. 미카 인 코리아의 44번째 비디오를 봐 주셔서 감사합니다. 이번 영상에서 저는 같이 한국어 수업을 들었던 친구 스튜를 만나서 부대찌개를 먹으러 갔어요. 한국어 공부의 어려움에 대해서 이야기를 나눠보고 발음하기 어려운 한국어 문장에도 도전을 해봤어요. 정말 재밌었고, 식당에 계신 아주머니들도 많이 웃으셨어요. ㅋㅋㅋ 스튜는 영국 런던 출신이고 몇 년 전 지금의 아내와 함께 살기 위해 한국으로 왔어요. 최근에 제가 한국어 공부를 많이 못했는데, 그 동안 스튜의 한국어는 더 늘었더라구요. 많은 자극을 받았고 앞으로 한국어를 더 열심히 공부해야겠다는 생각을 하게됐어요!

정말 더운 날이었지만 그래도 부대찌개는 너무 맛있었어요. 날이 더워서 그냥 소주 말고 상큼한 자몽 소주를 한두잔 했답니다. 오늘 저희가 나눈 이야기가 여러분들께도 흥미로웠기를 바라고, 발음하기 어려운 한국어 문장에 도전한 저희 모습도 귀엽게 봐주세요. 혹시 여러분들 발음하기 어려운 독일어 문장에 대해서도 들어보고 싶으신가요? 댓글로 많은 의견 주세요.

아직 제 채널을 구독하지 않으셨다면, 꼭 구독 해 주세요!! 한국에서의 제 일상을 구경하시고 응원 해 주세요.

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to my 44th video of Mika in Korea. This time my old friend Stu joins me for a Budaejjigae Mukbang and we are talking about Korean language, why it is difficult for foreigners to learn and also trying to learn some Korean Tongue Twisters. Which was really funny for everybody who listened to us in the restaurant. Stu is originally from London / England and he moved to Korea two years ago to get live with his Korean wife. We met in the Language Course, where we both studies Korean for one year together. Stu studied Korean pretty well lately, unfortunately I didn’t have so much time to practise / study Korean but I promise I ll get to it very soon again!

Although it was really hot outside we enjoyed the Budaejjigae a lot. Also drinking 1-2 shots of Soju, what else :D We really hope you had fun listening to our versions of the Korean Tongue Twisters. Perhaps you are interested in some funny German words and Tongue Twisters as well? Please let me know in the comment section! kkkkk

snippet.title: Difference between Korean and International Marriage 👩‍❤️‍👨 Bossam (보쌈) Mukbang (Mika in Korea 043)
snippet.description:
Subscribe Mika in Korea 🇦🇹 🇰🇷 for more Videos https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCehQUCosGefZu2xG_cqqLDA?sub_confirmation=1
and follow me on Instagram https://www.instagram.com/mikainkorea/
And follow Daldal.tv for some couple content: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCt4Dm5x9HODOUr-nbnlT_Ng?sub_confirmation=1

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - 

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to my 43th video of Mika in Korea. This time I met up with my dear friend Dominic from Dom & Hyo and we went to Hongdae to eat some delicious Bossam and enjoy our Friday night. And literally TGIF, since Dom and also me had a pretty rough week behind us and we were both looking forward to enjoy some good food and a few shots of Soju! At the end we decided to order 2 bottles of Soju, so everybody got his own bottle and we really had fun drinking it.

For everybody who doesn’t know what Bossam is. It is a super popular pork dish / pork wrap in Korean cuisine. The meat is served with side dishes such as spicy radish salad, sliced raw garlic, ssamjang (wrap sauce), saeu-jeot (salted shrimp), kimchi, and ssam (wrap) vegetables such as lettuce, kkaennip (perilla leaves), and inner leaves of a napa cabbage. Basically the perfect Korean anju, what means food accompanying alcoholic drinks! To eat the meat you have to wrap it up in a leave together with all the ingredients and eat it with one bite! „bossam“ literally means "wrapped" or "packaged" in Korean.

Besides enjoying this delicious Bossam with Soju, we also talked about the differences about Korean and International marriages! Since Dom and I are both married to Korean woman and we went a lot of time to Korean weddings, we compared in which ways Koreans are different than us westerners. So we talked about how Korean families are different to the USA and Austria, also why they don’t take over the husband’s name, the pressure on a Korean couple after getting married, sharing their income together, making presents to Korean and western parents and how much influence Korean parents take in an marriage as well.

We really had a looooot of fun shooting this video and somehow it is less a mukbang but more a sulbang, a video where it is more about drinking and having a fun time. I am happy that Dom joined me for this video and I hope he will join me soon again!

As usually, if you didn’t subscribe to my Youtube channel yet, I would be super duper happy, if you would do so! Follow me on my adventures here as a foreigner living in South Korea. Again, thank you soooo much for watching, I truly appreciate. 다음에 또 만나요. 안녕!

ko.title: 한국의 결혼생활 vs. 외국의 결혼생활 👩‍❤️‍👨 "보쌈 + 소주" 외국인 먹방 술방 반응 (미카인코리아 043)
ko.description:
더 많은 비디오를 원하시면 Mika in Korea를 구독 해 주세요 https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCehQUCosGefZu2xG_cqqLDA?sub_confirmation=1

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - 

안녕하세요, 여러분. 미카인코리아의 43번째 비디오를 봐주셔서 감사합니다. 이번엔 돔앤효의 도미닉을 만나 연남동에서 유명한 모듬 보쌈 맛집을 갔어요. 금요일 저녁이었고 저나 도미닉 모두 힘든 한 주를 보낸 뒤였기때문에 맛있는 음식에 술을 한 잔 하는 걸 정말 기대하고 갔답니다. 날이 날이다보니 소주는 각 1병으로 주문한 뒤 맛있는 저녁식사를 시작했어요.

저는 평소에도 보쌈을 좋아하는데요 여러가지 채소와 고기를 함께 먹을 수 있는 요리라 정말 좋은 것 같아요. 보쌈은 역시 쌈을 싸먹어야 맛있는데 저는 상추파, 도미닉은 깻잎파에요. 채소에 고기, 쌈장, 마늘을 넣고 한 입 싸서 넣으니 말 그래도 술이 술술 들어가더라구요. 특히 이 식당에는 돼지고기 보쌈만 나오는 게 아니라, 훈제 오리고기와 순대까지 나와서 더 먹을 게 많았던 것 같아요.

맛있는 보쌈에 소주 한 잔을 하며 우리는 한국의 결혼생활과 외국의 결혼생활에 대해서 이야기를 나눴어요. 돔도 저도 한국인과 결혼을 해서 한국식 결혼식을 한 경험이 있기때문에 한국의 결혼식, 가족의 관계, 결혼생활에서의 금전적인 관리 등이 어떻게 다른 나라와 다른지 이야기할 수 있었어요. 한국에서는 결혼 후에 배우자의 성을 따르지 않는 점이라든지, 수입을 같이 관리 한다든지, 가족끼리 현금을 선물한다든지, 하는 여러가지 이야기가 나왔어요. 내용이 궁금하신 분들은 비디오를 꼭 끝까지 봐주세요!!

정말 재밌는 시간을 보냈고, 먹방이라기보다는 술방에 가까운 비디오에요. 저희가 재밌었던만큼 보시는 분들도 재밌게 봐주시면 정말 행복할 것 같습니다. 제 비디오에 나와준 도미닉에게 다시 한 번 고맙다는 말을 하고 싶고, 다음에 또 나와주면 좋겠어요!

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - 

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to my 42th video of Mika in Korea. And wow, it really got sooo hot these days in South Korea. Especially for me the Korean summer is really tough because it isn’t just hot it is also super humid as well. Austrian summer is also hot these days but more easy going than Korean one. And since I am suffering so much these days because of the heat, my friend Alex and me decided to eat an iconic summer dish, which is super popular in Korea: Samgye-tang (삼계탕) or also called Korean Traditional Ginseng Chicken Soup! For people who don’t know what #Samgyetang is. It is a chicken stuffed with soaked sweet rice (aka glutinous rice). Garlic, ginger, and jujubes (dried red dates) are other common ingredients.

In Korea there are there days in the lunar calendar, which mark the hottest and most sultry summer days in Korea: Chobok (초복), Jungbok (중복) and Malbok (말복)! And Koreans believe, that eating samgyetang on these days promotes health and stamina! As the Korean saying goes, eating the hot soup is in the Korean summer is like “fighting the heat with heat.” And I have to say, I immediately felt better after eating this delicious Korean Ginseng Chicken Soup aka SamGyeTang (삼계탕). I am already looking forward to also eat Samgyetang Jungbok (중복) and Malbok (말복), to complete my SamGyeTang „quest“ :D Haha!

Besides eating the delicious Korean Traditional Ginseng Chicken Soup Alex and me talked about loosing weight in Korea, why it is so hard to do and what the differences are to Austria and the USA. It is really hard to loose weight, since Korea has such a hughe drinking and eating culture. So if you are Korean, how do you keep in shape meanwhile eating all the delicious Korean food and drinking so much as well. Please let me know!

As usually, if you didn’t subscribe to my Youtube channel yet, I would be super duper happy, if you would do so! Follow me on my adventures here as a foreigner living in South Korea. Again, thank you soooo much for watching, I truly appreciate. 다음에 또 만나요. 안녕!

안녕하세요, 여러분. 미카인코리아의 42번째 비디오를 봐 주셔서 감사합니다. 요즘 정말 덥지 않나요? 오스트리아의 여름은 한국처럼 습하지가 않아서 개인적으로 더운 여름날씨에 적응하는데 특히 애를 먹고 있어요. 더위 때문에 고생하고 있던 중 드디어 초복이 다가왔네요. 친구 알렉스와 함께 여름철 보양식인 삼계탕을 먹고 왔습니다. 

한국에는 초복, 중복, 말복, 총 세 번의 복날이 있다지요? 이렇게 더운 날 왜 뜨거운 삼계탕을 먹어야 하는지 처음에는 이해할 수 없었어요. 하지만 지금은 삼계탕이 얼마나 힘을 주는 음식인지 이해할 수 있답니다. “이열치열”의 의미를 이해하게 됐으니 한국문화를 조금 더 이해하게 된 걸까요? 다가오는 중복과 말복에도 맛있는 삼계탕을 먹을 생각에 벌써 설렙니다.

#삼계탕 을 먹으면서 알렉스와 다이어트에 대해서 이야기를 나눴어요. 실은 알렉스와 제가 다이어트 중이거든요. 살을 빼는 건 그 자체로 힘든 일이지만, 한국에서 살을 빼는 건 특히 힘들 때가 있어요. 오스트리아, 미국과 비교해서 한국에서 다이어트 하는데 특히 힘든 점은 어떤 게 있는지 이야기를 나누었으니 내용이 궁금하신 분들께서는 비디오를 끝까지 봐 주세요. 그리고 이렇게 맛있는 음식과 술을 많이 먹으면서도 날씬한 한국 구독자 여러분들께 비결이 뭔지 여쭤보고 싶어요. 맛있는 걸 먹고도 날씬한 몸매를 유지하는 비결이 있으시다면 댓글로 좀 알려주세요!

아직 제 채널을 구독하지 않으셨다면, 꼭 구독 해 주세요!! 한국에서의 제 일상을 구경하시고 응원 해 주세요.
제 비디오를 봐 주셔서 정말 감사합니다. 다음에 또 만나요. 안녕!

snippet.title: 5 difficulties for foreigners living in South Korea 🇰🇷 Gopchang Jeongol Mukbang (Mika in Korea 041)
snippet.description:
Subscribe Mika in Korea 🇦🇹 🇰🇷 for more Videos https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCehQUCosGefZu2xG_cqqLDA?sub_confirmation=1
and follow me on Instagram https://www.instagram.com/mikainkorea/
And follow Daldal.tv for some couple content: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCt4Dm5x9HODOUr-nbnlT_Ng?sub_confirmation=1

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - 

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to my 41th video of Mika in Korea. This time we went to visit my good friend Tomek and his wife in Yongin (용인), where they invited me to eat some local specialities: Gopchang-jeongol (곱창전골), or beef tripe hot pot and this is a spicy Korean stew or casserole made by boiling beef tripe, vegetables, and seasonings in beef broth. Basically beef intestines! There is also something similiar in Austrian and Polish culture but I was never into intestines. But this time I wanted to try something new, so we went to eat some Gopchang (곱창)! The first bites felt a little bit wired but with time I got used to it and I kinda enjoyed it. Tomek was really into it, it is one of his favorite Korean food.

Besides eating Gopchang-jeongol (곱창전골) we also talked about difficulties for foreigners living in South Korea. Of course withhout learning the language everything would be difficult for us but we tried to focus on topics, that a generel a little bit inconvenient for us foreigners. For example, my full name is too long for Korean system, so I can’t get a pointcard in the supermarket. Also finding Western style breakfast isn’t easy in Korea. Also it is difficult for taller people to live in Korea and to make friends with Korean people, if you don’t work in a Korean company. If you have something to add up, I am curious about your difficulties and experiences as a foreigner here in Korea. Please let me know them in the comments!

As usually, if you didn’t subscribe to my Youtube channel yet, I would be super duper happy, if you would do so! Follow me on my adventures here as a foreigner living in South Korea. Again, thank you soooo much for watching, I truly appreciate. 다음에 또 만나요. 안녕!

and follow me on Instagram https://www.instagram.com/mikainkorea/

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to my 41th video of Mika in Korea. This time we went to visit my good friend Tomek and his wife in Yongin (용인), where they invited me to eat some local specialities: Gopchang-jeongol (곱창전골), or beef tripe hot pot and this is a spicy Korean stew or casserole made by boiling beef tripe, vegetables, and seasonings in beef broth. Basically beef intestines! There is also something similiar in Austrian and Polish culture but I was never into intestines. But this time I wanted to try something new, so we went to eat some Gopchang (곱창)! The first bites felt a little bit wired but with time I got used to it and I kinda enjoyed it. Tomek was really into it, it is one of his favorite Korean food.

Besides eating Gopchang-jeongol (곱창전골) we also talked about difficulties for foreigners living in South Korea. Of course withhout learning the language everything would be difficult for us but we tried to focus on topics, that a generel a little bit inconvenient for us foreigners. For example, my full name is too long for Korean system, so I can’t get a pointcard in the supermarket. Also finding Western style breakfast isn’t easy in Korea. Also it is difficult for taller people to live in Korea and to make friends with Korean people, if you don’t work in a Korean company. If you have something to add up, I am curious about your difficulties and experiences as a foreigner here in Korea. Please let me know them in the comments!

As usually, if you didn’t subscribe to my Youtube channel yet, I would be super duper happy, if you would do so! Follow me on my adventures here as a foreigner living in South Korea. Again, thank you soooo much for watching, I truly appreciate. 다음에 또 만나요. 안녕!

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to my 40th video of Mika in Korea. This time I met up with my good old friend Paul and we went together to a famous Kimchi Jjigae Restaurant in Seoul, which was even featured on Korean TV. Kimchijjigae (김치찌개) is my favorite Korean food next to Dakgalbi, so I was really looking forward to try this local Kimchi Jjigae place. For the ones, who don’t know what Kimchi Jjigae is: Kimchi stew is one of the most-loved of all the stews in Korean cuisine. It’s a warm, hearty, spicy, savory, delicious dish that pretty much everyone loves. As long as they can handle spicy food, I never met a person who didn’t like kimchi-jjigae. Even Paul, who isn’t as good with spicy Korean food could enjoy this delicious Kimchi Jjigae!

Besides eating Kimchi Jjigae (김치찌개), we also talked about 5 things foreigners love about Korea. So we brought up topics like Korean food, that meals in Korea are way cheaper than abroad, that everything is quick here, so you don’t need to wait for anything, like for example for the internet setup. Also we talked about the ultimate convenience of living in South Korea and also the Korean medical care system. Of course there are many more things, foreigners like about living in Korea, but these are our 5 shorts points and insights.

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to my 39th video of Mika in Korea. Today the charming Lara is joining me for a delicious Korean Spicy Stir-Fried Chicken Mukbang or just simply a Dakgalbi mukbang. Most of you will know Lara from her own Youtube channel LaraLand 라라랜드 or from 코리안브로스 Korean Bros, where Lara is one of the main guests. And I am happy to welcome Lara to my channel today and we really had a loooot of fun eating Dakgalbi. Of course it isn’t the first time eating Dakgalbi for us but for both of us it was the first time eating a special version of Dakgalbi, called sutbul / charcoal Dakgalbi (숯불 닭갈비). A user recommanded this to us so of course we went out and looked for a place in Seoul, where they offer this delicious Dakgalbi. Of course I couldn’t resist drinking some Makgeolli (막걸리) with the Korean chicken dish but it really was just one bottle, for the taste! No day drinking / 낮술 madness like in the other videos :D Besides drinking and eating Korean food we also talk about the charms of Korean people to us foreigners, about our relationship with our in-law-parents, which is totally different than in a Korean Drama / K-Drama! We really had a great time together and I really hope Lara will come back soon again so we can talk more about everything!

As usually, if you didn’t subscribe to my Youtube channel yet, I would be super duper happy, if you would do so! Follow me on my adventures here as a foreigner living in South Korea. Again, thank you soooo much for watching, I truly appreciate. 다음에 또 만나요. 안녕!

안녕하세요, 여러분. 미카인코리아의 39번째 비디오를 봐 주셔서 감사합니다. 오늘은 숯불닭갈비 맛집에서 먹방을 했어요. 아마 많은 분들이 코리안브로스의 라라(라라랜드)를 잘 알고 계실텐데요, 라라가 저희 동네에 놀러를 왔어요.

닭갈비라는 음식을 처음 먹어본 것은 아니었지만 여태까지 먹은 닭갈비는 철판닭갈비였는데 숯불닭갈비는 제게 닭갈비의 신세계를 열어주었답니다. 지난 비디오에서 댓글로 숯불닭갈비를 추천 해 주신 분이 계셨는데 덕분에 정말 잘 먹었어요!! 또 이렇게 맛있는 음식을 먹으면서 또 막걸리를 한 잔 안 할 수가 없겠죠? ㅋㅋ 다른 영상에서처럼 취할 때까지 마시진 않았지만 막걸리를 마시면서 라라와 이런저런 재미있는 이야기를 나누었답니다.

저희가 생각한 한국 사람들의 매력, 한국 드라마와는 달랐던 실제 한국의 고부관계 등, 흥미로운 이야기들이니 꼭 끝까지 봐 주세요! 정말 재밌는 시간이었고, 다음에 라라가 또 놀러오면 더 재밌는 이야기들을 들려드릴게요.

snippet.title: Korean International Couple watches Korea 🇰🇷 vs. Sweden 🇸🇪 | Chimaek Mukbang (Mika in Korea 038)
snippet.description:
Subscribe Mika in Korea 🇦🇹 🇰🇷 for more Videos https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCehQUCosGefZu2xG_cqqLDA?sub_confirmation=1
and follow me on Instagram https://www.instagram.com/mikainkorea/
And follow Daldal.tv for some couple content: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCt4Dm5x9HODOUr-nbnlT_Ng?sub_confirmation=1

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - 

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to my 38th video of Mika in Korea. And this time we stayed at home and watched the soccer game between Korea 🇰🇷 vs. Sweden 🇸🇪 in der first round of the World Cup 2018! Sujin and I ordered some chicken, so we wanted to enjoy some chimaek at home and enjoy the soccer match. Unfortunately the chicken delivery took hours on that evening, since every Korean seemed to order some chicken for the World Cup match. So after more than two hours later we finally got to eat our Korean fried chicken! In a convenient store I found some Austrian beer, called radler, which is a mix of beer and limonade. It just has 2,5% of alcohol in it, so very easy going. Unfortunately Korea lost against Sweden but we still hope Korea has a chance to succeed to the 2nd round. Although Mexico and Germany will be very very tough opponents! Let’s cross fingers. We really hope, you will like the reaction of a Korean international couple watching a soccer game. Unfortunately Austria is out of the championship, so I can only cheer for South Korea or Poland. We had a great time cheering for Korea and we are sad, that they lost because of a penalty shot! Next game will be better hopefully!

As usually, if you didn’t subscribe to my Youtube channel yet, I would be super duper happy, if you would do so! Follow me on my adventures here as a foreigner living in South Korea. Again, thank you soooo much for watching, I truly appreciate. 다음에 또 만나요. 안녕!

ko.title: 치맥과 함께하는 국제커플의 월드컵 응원 | 대한민국 🇰🇷 vs. 스웨덴 🇸🇪 | 외국인 치맥 먹방 (미카인코리아 038)
ko.description:
더 많은 비디오를 원하시면 Mika in Korea를 구독 해 주세요 https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCehQUCosGefZu2xG_cqqLDA?sub_confirmation=1

안녕하세요, 여러분. 미카인코리아의 38번째 비디오를 봐 주셔서 감사합니다. 월드컵이 시작되었는데요, 한국의 월드컵 본선 첫 경기인 대한민국 대 스웨덴 전을 아내와 함께 보기로 했습니다. 밖에 나가서 응원을 하는 대신 집에서 치맥을 먹으면서 응원을 하기로 했는데, 역시 스포츠 경기가 있는 날 치맥을 먹는 것이 쉬운 일은 아니었어요. 2시간도 더 넘어서 드디어 받은 치킨.. 늦은 시간에 먹어서 그런지 더 맛있더라구요.

얼마 전에 편의점에서 오스트리아 회사가 만든 "라들러" 맥주를 발견해서 사 두었는데 이 날 치킨과 함께 먹으니 정말 꿀맛이었어요. 알콜 도수도 2.5% 밖에 안 되어서 취하지 않고 경기에 집중 하면서 치킨도 즐길 수 있었답니다. 

안타깝게도 이 날 경기에서 한국이 스웨덴에 패했지만 멕시코와의 두번째 경기에서 좋은 결과가 있기를 바래봅니다. 멕시코와 독일 모두 쉬운 상대는 아니지만 기적은 언제든 일어날 수 있잖아요!! 제 조국인 오스트리아는 본선 진출도 하지 못했는데 대신 아내의 나라이자 제가 살고 있는 삶의 터전인 한국을 응원할 수 있어서 정말 뜻깊고 행복합니다. 저희의 치맥 먹방, 월드컵 리액션 비디오를 재밌게 봐 주시길 바랍니다. 다음 경기도 함께 응원해요!!!

아직 제 채널을 구독하지 않으셨다면, 꼭 구독 해 주세요!! 한국에서의 제 일상을 구경하시고 응원 해 주세요.

안녕하세요, 여러분. 미카인코리아의 37번째 비디오를 봐 주셔서 감사합니다. 지난 비디오에서 돼지국밥으로 해장을 한 뒤 다시 제대로 된 먹방 비디오를 찍을 수 있게 됐어요. 많은 분들이 친절하게 가르쳐 주신 해장음식은 차차 먹어보도록 할게요.

이번에는 파키스탄에서 온 친구 샤룬을 초대해서 문래동에 있는 유명한 돼지불백 (돼지불고기백반)을 먹으러 갔어요. 밥을 먹으면서 간단한 게임을 했는데요, 최근에 “한입만” 이라는 티비 프로그램을 봤던 샤룬이 한입만 게임을 해 보자고 하더라구요. 그래서 돼지불고기 쌈을 최대한 크게 싸서 상대방이 싼 쌈을 한 입에 먹는 게임을 했어요. 샤룬과 저 중에 누가 게임에 이겼는지 궁금하시죠? 그럼 비디오를 끝까지 봐 주세요. 신선한 채소에 밥과 고기 등 여러 가지 반찬을 넣고 싸먹는 쌈 요리는 저도 참 좋아하는 한국 요리에요. 또 저희는 각자가 좋아하는 한국 음식들에 대해서도 이야기를 나누었어요. 샤룬과 정말 재밌는 시간을 보냈고 돼지불백도 정말 맛있게 먹었답니다.

아직 제 채널을 구독하지 않으셨다면, 꼭 구독 해 주세요!! 한국에서의 제 일상을 구경하시고 응원 해 주세요.

snippet.title: Dwaeji Gukbap 🐷 Korean Hangover Pork and Rice Soup after a wild party night (Mika in Korea 036)
snippet.description:
Subscribe Mika in Korea 🇦🇹 🇰🇷 for more Videos https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCehQUCosGefZu2xG_cqqLDA?sub_confirmation=1
and follow me on Instagram https://www.instagram.com/mikainkorea/
And follow Daldal.tv for some couple content: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCt4Dm5x9HODOUr-nbnlT_Ng?sub_confirmation=1

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - 

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to my 36th video of Mika in Korea. And yeah, this time my good friend Cedric and I went to eat some delicious Dwaeji Gukbap, what is some kind of Korean Hangover Soup, after we had a very, very rough night celebrating our friend’s birthday party! Dwaeji Gukbap is a Pork and Rice Soup and is originally a specialty dish from Busan, which is relatively unknown and rare in Seoul, but we found a place in Hapjeong, where they served a really good Dwaeji Gukbap (돼지국밥). The special thing about Dwaeji Gukbap is, that it is a high maintenance recipe as it takes hours of boiling the pork bone to get the milk-coloured broth. Usually it is encouraged for women after childbirth and for the weak, or for people who went out all night long and came back home early in the morning kkkk. Like us! We also talked about Hangover drinks and food in the USA and in Austria and what differences there are. Also I found out, that the famous Austrian „Reparaturseidl“ also exists in South Korea, being called Haejangsul (해장술). But this time I didn’t drink anything, because my stomache could barely handle the food. We really enjoyed our Korean Hangover Soup Dwaeji Gukbap and we definitely felt immediately way better after finishing the Busan specialty dish!

As usually, if you didn’t subscribe to my Youtube channel yet, I would be super duper happy, if you would do so! Follow me on my adventures here as a foreigner living in South Korea. Again, thank you soooo much for watching, I truly appreciate. 다음에 또 만나요. 안녕!

돼지국밥은 제 아내의 고향이기도한 부산 음식이라지요? 원조 부산 돼지국밥은 다음에 부산에 놀러 갔을 때 다시 먹어보기로 하고 이번에는 합정에 있는 돼지국밥 집에를 갔습니다. 이 곳도 아주 맛있었어요. 진짜 오랜 시간 돼지 뼈를 고아서 우유 빛깔의 육수를 내는 음식이라는 점이 저에겐 정말 신기하답니다. 설명을 찾아보니 산모나, 허약체질, 그리고 밤새 놀다 온 저 같은 사람에게 추천하는 음식이라고 하네요. ㅋㅋㅋ

세디와 함께 미국과 오스트리아에도 한국처럼 숙취해소 음료가 있는지, 사람들이 어떻게 해장을 하는지 등에 대해 이야기를 나눴어요. 그리고 오스트리아에서 유명한 „Reparaturseidl“이 한국에도 있다는 사실을 발견했는데 한국어로는 해장술이라고 한대요. 아쉽게도 이번에는 해장술을 먹을 수가 없었어요. 속이 너무 안 좋았거든요. 한국식 해장 음식인 돼지국밥, 정말 맛있게 먹었구요, 이 참에 부산에 가서도 먹방 쫌 찍어야겠어요.

아직 제 채널을 구독하지 않으셨다면, 꼭 구독 해 주세요!! 한국에서의 제 일상을 구경하시고 응원 해 주세요.

snippet.title: Korean BBQ 🇰🇷 Foreigners enjoying Galmaegisal Mukbang with Soju (Mika in Korea 035)
snippet.description:
Subscribe Mika in Korea 🇦🇹 🇰🇷 for more Videos https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCehQUCosGefZu2xG_cqqLDA?sub_confirmation=1
and follow me on Instagram https://www.instagram.com/mikainkorea/
And follow Daldal.tv for some couple content: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCt4Dm5x9HODOUr-nbnlT_Ng?sub_confirmation=1

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - 

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to my 35th video of Mika in Korea. For this Mukbang episode I met up with my French friend Sebastian, who moved to Sindorim not long ago and it was time, to finally do something together again. We decided to eat some traditional Korean BBQ, more specifically skirt meat or skirt steak, called Galmaegisal. There is a really good place we both like in Sindorim, so we decided to go there. Of course we can’t just eat skirt steak without any booze or Korean alcohol, for Korean BBQ Soju is a must-have on the table! These days I am really a lot into Somek (소맥), some kind of beer cocktail made with soju and beer! I also practised my Soju Mixing in that video, thx for my Korean cousine for teaching me that :D Also we talk about, why foreigners like Korean BBQ so much and generally about different food cultures and etiquettes. We really had a lot of fun, unfortunately I drank a little bit too much Somek at the end, so I got a little tipsy and crazy at the end. But it just shows, that we really enjoyed our Galmaegisal BBQ and that we had a great time. If you are interested, what Sebastian is doing, check out his Youtube Channel Seboom, where he is having a Live Streaming Show about K-Pop music!

As usually, if you didn’t subscribe to my Youtube channel yet, I would be super duper happy, if you would do so! Follow me on my adventures here as a foreigner living in South Korea. Again, thank you soooo much for watching, I truly appreciate. 다음에 또 만나요. 안녕!

ko.description:
더 많은 비디오를 원하시면 Mika in Korea를 구독 해 주세요 https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCehQUCosGefZu2xG_cqqLDA?sub_confirmation=1

snippet.title: Korean Gamjatang & Sundae Mukbang 🍲 Afterwork Dinner with friends (Mika in Korea 034)
snippet.description:
Subscribe Mika in Korea 🇦🇹 🇰🇷 for more Videos https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCehQUCosGefZu2xG_cqqLDA?sub_confirmation=1
and follow me on Instagram https://www.instagram.com/mikainkorea/
And follow Daldal.tv for some couple content: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCt4Dm5x9HODOUr-nbnlT_Ng?sub_confirmation=1

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - 

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to my 34th video of Mika in Korea. This time we spontanously decided to eat dinner together and went to a Traditional Korean Restaurant, where they served some delicious Korean Gamjatang and Sundae. Gamjatang (감자탕) is a spicy Korean pig neck stew with potatoes inside and Sundae (순대) is a spicy Korean blood sausage. We didn’t plan to shoot a mukbang video on that evening, so the material is raw but I think it is still interesting and fun to watch. Together with my friend Michin Alex and his friend Frankie (perhaps you know him from the Amercian K-Pop Band EXP EDITION (이엑스피 에디션) we really enjoyed the Gamjatang and Sundae. Also we had one bottle of makgeolli (막걸리) which fit perfectly to this late Korean dinner! I personally like Gamjatang a lot and Sundae reminds me of the Austrian bloody sausage called „Blutwurst“.

As usually, if you didn’t subscribe to my Youtube channel yet, I would be super duper happy, if you would do so! Follow me on my adventures here as a foreigner living in South Korea. Again, thank you soooo much for watching, I truly appreciate. 다음에 또 만나요. 안녕!

안녕하세요 여러분 and welcome to my 34th video of Mika in Korea. This time we spontanously decided to eat dinner together and went to a Traditional Korean Restaurant, where they served some delicious Korean Gamjatang and Sundae. Gamjatang (감자탕) is a spicy Korean pig neck stew with potatoes inside and Sundae (순대) is a spicy Korean blood sausage. We didn’t plan to shoot a mukbang video on that evening, so the material is raw but I think it is still interesting and fun to watch. Together with my friend Michin Alex and his friend Frankie (perhaps you know him from the Amercian K-Pop Band EXP EDITION (이엑스피 에디션) we really enjoyed the Gamjatang and Sundae. Also we had one bottle of makgeolli (막걸리) which fit perfectly to this late Korean dinner! I personally like Gamjatang a lot and Sundae reminds me of the Austrian bloody sausage called „Blutwurst“.

ko.description:

안녕하세요, 여러분. 미카인코리아의 34번째 브이로그에 오신 걸 환영합니다. 이번 브이로그는 친구들과 저녁을 먹으러 갔다가 계획 없이 촬영했는데요, 늦은 시간에 사람들이 많이 가는 24시간 감자탕집을 가 봤어요. 야근을 마치고, 혹은 밤새 일을 해야하는 어중간한 시간에 배고픈 사람들의 허기를 달래주는 감자탕 집.. 이 곳에서 뜨끈한 감자탕 국물에 뭐든 한 잔 하는 그 맛이야 말로 인생의 맛 아니겠습니까.

감자탕은 돼지의 '감자'라는 부위로 만든 국물 요리이고 순대는 한국식 "피 소세지"입니다. 이 날은 촬영을 할 계획이 없었고 다들 피곤하기도 해서 비디오가 뭔가 더 날 것의 느낌이 있기는 하지만 재미있게 만들었으니 많이 봐 주세요. 미친 알렉스와 알렉스의 친구 프랭키 (아실지 모르겠지만 이엑스피 에디션이라는 외국인들로 구성된 케이팝 그룹 출신의 아이돌이랍니다.)와 함께 감자탕에 순대볶음을 맛있게 먹었어요. 제가 좋아하는 막걸리도 한 병 시켜서 같이 먹었는데요, 막걸리는 모든 한국 음식과 잘 어울리는 것 같아요. 감자탕은 정말 맛있었고 순대볶음은 오스트리아 요리 „Blutwurst“ ("피 소시지")가 생각 나더라구요. 일이 남아서 빨리 먹고 돌아가야했지만 그래도 정말 재미있는 저녁이었습니다.
